messages.subject: Re: more comments on the stan manual
parts:
Thanks.

On 8/15/12 4:55 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> B
> I have a bunch of comments. I could also edit the latex file if that would be easier. I like the overall structure but I'd move things around a bit.
> A
>
> - cover page: maybe we should have the url, http://mc-stan.org right there on the cover and elsewhere in the document. I recall you saying that some people will see the manual and not the webpage, so maybe the manual shoudl point to the webpage very clearly.

That totally makes sense. I just did that.

> - p.2: "p(theta|y;x)": the semicolon should be a comma.

I know Andrew likes to overload single symbols like commas
for multiple purposes. Here, I was using the semicolon to
distinguish what is and what isn't being modeled as random.
In p(theta|y;x), the x is NOT being modeled as random, it's
a predictor. Nothing in the model ever gives it a probability
model.



> - Section 1.5, first displayed equation should be p(θ|y,x) ∝ p(y|θ, x) p(θ| x). There are no semicolons in Bayesian inference!
> Similarly, these should be fixed in the following lines.

I understand it should be consistent.
>
> - Many page numbers are still missing. I'm surprised this is a problem; I typically have no problems getting page numbers in Latex documents. Maybe you could ask Malecki for help?

That was an errant pagestyle in the intro. I just
fixed it late last night, but haven't uploaded a new one.

> - I think Sections 2.4 thru 2.10 should go later. These are important techncial matters but they are not necessary to get started. Instead it will be fine to point to the url for the Getting Started webpage and then put these sections inside Section 3 and elseqwhere where they fit better.

Eh? Are we looking at the same doc?

2.1 is installation, which you want expanded
into point-by-point by operating system.

2.2 is just an example of a minimal no-data program without
any instructions on how to run it.

2.3 is just about semicolons and whitespace.

I wouldn't call it "getting started" if it doesn't
show you how to run a simple model!

2.4 unpacking Stan tarball
2.5 building stanc and libstan.a
2.6 running stanc to translate a model from .stan to .cpp
2.7 compiling the .cpp model
2.8 running sampling on the compiled model
2.9 inspecting the output format
2.10 providing data
2.11 proper/improper priors [this I could see moving]
2.12 comments

These "technical matters" you want to move elsewhere are
already fully covered elsewhere. They're just a simple
walkthrough of how to run Stan. Each one-paragraph section is expanded
on at chapter length in the reference manual part of the
manual.

> - Section 2.12: I'm confused about the first two paragraphs. Are # and // completely equivalent in Stan?

Yes.

> If so, perhaps it's enough to give the full story for // and then say that # will also work.

OK. But if we're getting rid of the section,
I won't need to do anything :-)

> Also, I was thinking it would help to have a section, Stan for Users of Bugs and Jags. I could try to write that section!

That'd be great. Presumably this would just be about the
models, not about the R interface, calling from the command
line, etc.

Will it be two sectiosn, one for BUGS and one for JAGS,
or will you interleave info from both? Their syntax isn't
the same -- it differs in multivariate ops, truncation syntax,
range of built-in functions, etc.

- Bob
